name: GitHub Copilot CLI

surfaces.label: copilot in a terminal. A native arm64/x64 Mach-O (Node single-executable app), not a node process. Homebrew cask symlinks /opt/homebrew/bin/copilot, install.sh writes ~/.local/bin/copilot or /usr/local/bin/copilot, npm runs node npm-loader.js which spawns .../@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot as a child (match the child, never the node parent). Also covers -p one-shot runs and --ui-server (TUI plus local server, optionally with --port N). NAME COLLISION: the AWS Copilot CLI (Homebrew formula 'copilot', end-of-support 2026-06-12) also installs a binary named copilot at the same path, so a name match alone is not proof. Confirm with ~/.copilot/session-state/*/inuse.<pid>.lock or ~/.copilot/logs/process-<timestamp>-<pid>.log for the pid.

GitHub Copilot desktop app (Tauri, installed at /Applications/GitHub Copilot.app). A separate product from the CLI. It hosts the Copilot runtime itself: it can spawn the CLI or the bundled copilot-runtime wrapper over TCP or stdio, and its Rust SDK also has an in-process transport, so children may not exist at all. That it shares the ~/.copilot session store is inferred (COPILOT_HOME defaults to ~/.copilot), not observed. The probe splits ps args on spaces, so this path never matches; detect the app by bundle id.
copilot --acp: Agent Client Protocol server, spawned by an editor (Zed, JetBrains and other ACP clients). Requires --stdio or --port N; stdio is the default when --port is absent.

copilot --server: headless JSON-RPC session server for the Copilot SDK (stdio or --port N TCP). The CLI itself spawns `--server --port 0 --managed-server` children behind a feature flag; the outermost-process rule in the probe folds those into their parent.
copilot --headless: alias of --server. The Copilot SDK and desktop app start the runtime as `<runtime> --headless --no-auto-update [--stdio | --port N]`.

copilot --ahp-host: headless AHP (agent host protocol) host, default listen 127.0.0.1:8765, awaits forever and may outlive the CLI that started it. Own log ahp-host-<pid>.log. New in 1.0.8x, not in the vendor docs.

copilot-runtime: the small Mach-O wrapper that the Copilot SDK and desktop app extract from the package (prebuilds/darwin-arm64/copilot-runtime) and start with --headless/--server. Not the copilot binary, so the names above do not cover it. Exact argv unverified.
Copilot cloud agent and remote sessions (--remote, --connect): same harness on GitHub-hosted Linux. No local process, no macOS signal.

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: Exact only when the user runs /keep-alive busy (setting keepAlive=busy): the CLI then spawns `caffeinate -dis -w <its own pid>` for the length of the turn. Default is keepAlive=off, so it is normally absent. In mode `on` or a timed keep-alive the child is held for the whole session including idle, so it is a false positive there.

working_signals.name: PreventUserIdleSystemSleep
working_signals.meaning: GUI surface only. The Copilot app process (com.github.githubapp) creates an IOPMAssertion 'GitHub Copilot app ... N active session(s)' while a session is busy, with a grace period after idle. Only when its Keep Awake setting is on. Default of that setting not determined.

events.jsonl is expected to get a line at user.message, assistant.turn_start, tool.execution_start/complete, assistant.message and assistant.turn_end: these are typed as not-always-transient (`ephemeral?: boolean`) in the SDK typings, but no real file was read. Events typed `ephemeral: true` (assistant.message_delta, assistant.usage, assistant.idle, session.idle, user_input.requested, elicitation.requested, exit_plan_mode.requested, tool.execution_partial_result, session.usage_info) are never written, so a long model stream or a long shell command can leave a quiet file during a live turn. The probe needs a session id and a plain interactive process carries none in argv; map pid to session dir through ~/.copilot/session-state/*/inuse.<pid>.lock (undocumented, Linux report only).
Inferred, not measured. The Ink TUI animates a spinner while a turn runs; idle is expected near 0 percent. A turn blocked on the network can sit below the floor.

waiting_signals.meaning: Fires asynchronously with notification_type permission_prompt (tool needs approval) or elicitation_dialog (agent asks the user). Also agent_idle, agent_completed, shell_completed, shell_detached_completed. Fire-and-forget.
Fires before the permission engine runs, so it also fires for calls that are then auto-approved. Not proof that a human is being asked.
Main agent finished a turn and is back at the prompt. Pair with userPromptSubmitted for exact busy windows.

Terminal side, not visible to ps. OSC 9;4;3 (indeterminate progress) while the agent works and OSC 9;4;0 when it stops. Setting terminalProgress, default true. Rendered by iTerm2, Ghostty, Windows Terminal, ConEmu.
Terminal side. OSC 0 title carries the current intent (setting updateTerminalTitle, default true). No documented idle/working/waiting vocabulary in the title.

session.idle (transient, never on disk) marks the turn end for SDK, --server and --ui-server clients. permission.requested, user_input.requested, elicitation.requested and exit_plan_mode.requested mark waiting; the last three are transient. Needs a live connection to the CLI's own server, which is intrusive, so not used here.

hooks.config: JSON with {"version":1,"hooks":{...}}. Loaded and merged from: /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/*.json (root-owned, cannot be disabled), .github/hooks/*.json in the repo, ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json ($COPILOT_HOME/hooks), a hooks block in .github/copilot/settings.json or settings.local.json, a hooks block in ~/.copilot/settings.json, plugin hooks.json. Cross-tool .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json in the repo are also read. Command, http and prompt (sessionStart only) hook types.

telemetry.how: Off by default. Enabled by COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED=true, or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, or COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH (JSONL file). Exporter otlp-http (http/json default, http/protobuf optional) or file. service.name github-copilot. One invoke_agent root span per user message with chat and execute_tool children; gen_ai.conversation.id is the session id. Prompt and response content is off unless OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true. Also settable by the enterprise managed-settings telemetry block.

sources.claim: npm package @github/copilot is a tiny loader (12,968 bytes unpacked, npm-loader.js itself 1,185 bytes): bin copilot -> npm-loader.js, which spawnSync()s the native @github/copilot-<platform>-<arch> binary with stdio inherit. So under npm there is a node parent and a native child.

sources.claim: The native package is a Node single-executable app: one Mach-O binary that embeds copilot.tgz (index.js, app.js, runtime.node), extracts it to a pkg cache and import()s index.js inside the same process. No node child. Auto-update packages are loaded the same way, so the process stays the native copilot binary.
sources.evidence: Downloaded https://registry.npmjs.org/@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/-/copilot-darwin-arm64-1.0.89.tgz into the scratchpad (not executed). `file package/copilot` -> 'Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64'; `strings` shows NODE_SEA_FUSE_fce680ab2cc467b6e072b8b5df1996b2 and sea-loader.js with `await import(pathToFileURL(r))`, the extraction cache is COPILOT_PKG_CACHE_HOME|COPILOT_CACHE_HOME|~/Library/Caches/copilot + /pkg/darwin-arm64/1.0.89 (function Wi in sea-loader.js), with $COPILOT_HOME/pkg and ~/.copilot/pkg as fallback lookups Verifier re-extracted the embedded copilot.tgz from the binary and confirmed sea-loader.js loads index.js in-process via `await import(pathToFileURL(r))` and contains no spawn of node.

sources.claim: Session history lives in ~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/ with events.jsonl plus workspace artifacts; COPILOT_HOME or --config-dir moves ~/.copilot. session-store.db is a SQLite cross-session index (rebuilt by /chronicle reindex). logs/ holds process-{timestamp}-{pid}.log, one per process. Only the pid is in the log file name; the docs do not say the log holds the session id, so the log is a pid marker, not a pid to session map.
sources.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference (sections session-state/, session-store.db, logs/)

sources.claim: Each live process drops session-state/<id>/inuse.<pid>.lock containing only its pid. This is the pid to session map when argv has no id. Files are left behind after crashes, so check the pid is alive. Undocumented.
sources.evidence: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2609 (user report on 1.0.21, Linux only: 'Multiple stale inuse.[pid].lock files ... Each file contains only its PID'). Corroborated by the string 'inuse.' next to 'held session lock files mutex poisoned' in prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node of 1.0.89.

sources.claim: The CLI spawns `caffeinate -dis -w <process.pid>` on macOS (systemd-inhibit on Linux) as its keep-alive. It is opt-in: setting keepAlive is "off" by default, "busy" holds it only while the agent works, "on" or a duration holds it for the session. Slash command /keep-alive (alias /caffeinate).
sources.evidence: app.js in @github/copilot-darwin-arm64@1.0.89 (embedded copilot.tgz): class with startChildProcessKeepAlive({command:"caffeinate",args:["-dis","-w",String(process.pid)]}) and command /keep-alive with choices on|off|busy; docs: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference row keepAlive default "off"

notes: Documented and source-read, never observed running. Verified 2026-09-29 by an independent pass, see registry/evidence/copilot-cli.md ## Verification. Things that differ from the Claude Code row. (1) Only the exact `session.idle` event marks turn end and it is never written to disk, so the transcript cannot say idle; use hooks (userPromptSubmitted -> agentStop) for exact windows. (2) caffeinate is opt-in and can be held while idle, so it is not a safe standalone turn signal. (3) The interactive process has no session id in argv; map pid to session with ~/.copilot/session-state/*/inuse.<pid>.lock (undocumented, one Linux report on 1.0.21 plus an 'inuse.' string in runtime.node). The process log name process-<timestamp>-<pid>.log gives the pid only. (4) The name `copilot` is shared with the AWS Copilot CLI; the probe cannot tell them apart from argv, so a detector should also require a live inuse lock or process log for the pid. Excluding AWS subcommand words is not safe because the probe matches exclude_args against every space-separated token, prompt words included. (5) The probe splits ps args on spaces, so the GUI path '/Applications/GitHub Copilot.app/...' never matches; detect the app by bundle id com.github.githubapp. (6) `--resume=ID` and `--session-id=ID` (equals form, the form the CLI prints in its exit hint) are not read by the probe's session_id_args logic; a bare `--resume` makes the probe take the next argv as an id. (7) session_store.glob does not follow COPILOT_HOME or --config-dir. (8) A `copilot -p` run is a turn for its whole life but shows no caffeinate and may show low CPU. (9) SDK/app-hosted runtimes appear as `copilot-runtime`; if the SDK resolves a .js entry it runs `node <index.js>`, which no row here matches. Not determined: real ps args, CPU behaviour and child processes of a live TUI; the app's Keep Awake default.
